title: ChatGPT Business Profile: Claim It, Then Turn Clicks Into Customers - Klaviyo
summary: Claim your ChatGPT business profile in Business Hub, then turn AI-referred clicks into subscribers with targeted sign-up forms and a dedicated welcome flow.
body_markdown:
Turn ChatGPT discovery into owned customer relationships


Generated by Klaviyo AI


The article explains how eligible businesses can claim a ChatGPT profile, maintain product information, and review engagement insights. It outlines how Klaviyo forms, dedicated welcome flows, and on-site chat can help turn referred visitors into subscribers and customers, while noting limitations in referral tracking and access to ChatGPT conversations.


-


**Accurate business profiles:** Business Hub lets verified businesses update key details, add product feeds with pricing and availability, and review aggregated engagement insights.


-


**Separate customer relationships:** OpenAI does not share ChatGPT conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses, so owned relationships begin when visitors reach the business’s site and provide contact details.


-


**Tailored visitor experiences:** Klaviyo forms targeted by UTM parameters and dedicated welcome flows can offer AI-referred visitors relevant resources rather than a generic discount.


-


**On-site assistance:** Klaviyo Customer Agent answers product questions on the business’s site, and its conversation events can inform segments for identified shoppers.


-


**Referral tracking gaps:** ChatGPT does not reliably tag outbound links, so targeting a dedicated landing page URL can supplement UTM-based form targeting.

On Nov. 10, OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta that lets brands claim a profile, keep their information current, and see how people engage with them. And, there are a lot of people engaging with brands on ChatGPT. OpenAI says 1.2B people use ChatGPT *each week* .


Let's break down what OpenAI announced, why it matters, and what to set up in Klaviyo so a click from ChatGPT turns into a relationship you own.


## What is “Businesses in ChatGPT”?


OpenAI calls the launch[Businesses in ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/) . It has two parts, and both are in beta.


1. **Business Hub:** Verified businesses can update key details and add self-service product feeds with pricing and availability. Hub also shows aggregated insights: mentions, website clicks, and "discovery topics," the common themes in conversations that cite your site.
2. **Business Agents:** Eligible businesses can launch an agent that answers questions about their offerings. When a business appears in a ChatGPT response, people can open its profile and, if an agent exists, start a conversation. For now, agents are limited to eligible U.S. ecommerce and online service businesses.


OpenAI says it doesn't share users' conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses, and insights only appear once there's enough activity to meet certain thresholds.


## Why this matters for marketers


Think back to when organic search became a real channel. Brands that claimed their listings and kept their details accurate earned compounding traffic. Brands that waited and discounted organic search as a channel have spent years, perhaps decades, catching up.


[AI discovery](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/ai-search-trends) is on a similar path. Shoppers already ask assistants to compare products and narrow options, and a claimed profile gives you a say in what ChatGPT knows about you.


There's a second reason. When a shopper chats with a Business Agent, that conversation stays inside ChatGPT, and OpenAI doesn't share it with you. The relationship you can own starts when the shopper lands on your site and gives you a way to stay in touch. This means that any method you can use to get someone from ChatGPT to your site, and turn that visit into a customer, or at a minimum a subscriber on your owned channels (email, text messages, WhatsApp, or app), is worth the effort.


## Step 1: claim your business in ChatGPT


Any eligible business located where ChatGPT is available can claim a profile through Business Hub. Existing OpenAI Enterprise customers and advertisers can work with their OpenAI representative instead, and Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or the Shopify admin to streamline verification.


Once you're verified, focus on three things:


1. **Get the basics right:** Update your key details so they match what's on your site.
2. **Add a product feed:** Self-service feeds with pricing and availability give ChatGPT current information to work with, rather than a snapshot it found weeks ago.
3. **Check your insights:** Mentions, website clicks, and discovery topics show how ChatGPT represents you and where the gaps are.


Business Agents are optional and, for now, limited to eligible U.S. ecommerce and online service businesses. If you're eligible, decide deliberately, since the conversation stays in ChatGPT. Either way, make the path from your profile to your site the easiest next step.


## Step 2: welcome AI-referred visitors with Klaviyo


A shopper who clicks through from ChatGPT has often done their research already. A generic "10% off your first order" pop-up misses that moment. Here are three tactics you can use within KLaviyo to better personalize that experience.


### Customize sign-up forms for AI-referred traffic


[Target a form by UTM parameters](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/4413544555547-How-to-Choose-Form-Targeting-and-Behavior-Settings) so it only appears for visitors who arrive from ChatGPT. Lead with what they likely want next, like early access or a buying guide, instead of a standard discount, and raise its display priority so it beats your default welcome form.


Alternatively, test an[exit-intent form](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/exit-popups) instead of one that appears at the start of the visit. They may land further down the funnel than other traffic.


### Build a welcome flow that acknowledges how they found you


Send AI-referred sign-ups to their own list, or build a segment from the form they filled out, then trigger a[dedicated welcome flow](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002775172-How-to-create-an-email-welcome-series) . Open with why they came, point them to core brand information, best-sellers or a buying guide, and say what they'll get from you in their preferred channels.


### Point shoppers to your on-site chat


If you use Klaviyo[Customer Agent](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/customer-agent) , call it out in your form, welcome messages, and landing pages: "Not sure which fits? Ask our assistant." It learns from your storefront, catalog, and help content to answer product questions and recommend items. These shoppers are already comfortable with AI assistants, so pointing out your on-site chat may resonate.


One distinction worth making: a ChatGPT Business Agent lives in ChatGPT. Customer Agent lives on your site, where the relationship is yours, and for identified shoppers its[conversation events](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/44813293727131) can feed your segments.


## A note on tracking AI referrals


ChatGPT has added utm_source=chatgpt.com to many of its outbound links,[but not reliably](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/chatgpt-traffic-drop-appears-to-be-a-tracking-problem/593157/) . In October, analysts reported that tagged clicks dropped for about a week and showed up as direct traffic.


The practical takeaway is that a UTM-targeted form will catch tagged visits, not every ChatGPT visit. If you can send AI-referred shoppers to a dedicated landing page, you can also[target that URL](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/4413544555547-How-to-Choose-Form-Targeting-and-Behavior-Settings) and cover the gap.


## What to do this week


1. **Claim your business** in[Business Hub](https://openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/) and confirm your details and product feed are accurate.
2. **Check your analytics** for chatgpt.com traffic, including direct visits that may be untagged. (You can do this in[Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/ai-search-insights) , and for Shopify brands the same referral shows up in[Klaviyo](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/agentic-shopping-segmentation) as a UTM source.)
3. **Build a sign-up form** targeted to AI-referred visitors, and decide whether to stick with your current form strategy or test something new, like an exit-intent form.
4. **Set up a dedicated welcome flow** for those sign-ups.
5. **Turn on your on-site chat,** if it's available to you, and mention it in your form and welcome emails.


Business Hub helps ChatGPT represent you accurately. It doesn't give you the customer relationship. That part still happens on your site, in your forms, and in the messages you send after. Being found is step one. Being remembered is your actual job.
